questions.enonce_markdown:
Select from the elements (sodium, silver, calcium, iron and aluminium);

(i) A transition metal used as a catalyst.

(ii) An element that forms an amphoteric oxide.

(iii) An element that is a basic constituent of bones. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Iron (Fe)**: a transition metal; finely divided iron is the catalyst in the Haber process for ammonia.

(ii) **Aluminium (Al)**: aluminium oxide $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric.

(iii) **Calcium (Ca)**: bones and teeth are made mainly of calcium phosphate.

questions.enonce_markdown: Arrange the elements in order of decreasing reactivity, starting from the most reactive. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Order of the reactivity series: **sodium > calcium > aluminium > iron > silver** (Na > Ca > Al > Fe > Ag).

Sodium and calcium react with water, aluminium and iron react only with acids or steam, and silver does not react with dilute acids.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The element Calcium (Ca) reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid.

(i) State one common observation.

(ii) Write a balanced equation for the reaction taking place. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Effervescence**: bubbles of a colourless gas (hydrogen) are given off as the calcium dissolves; the mixture becomes warm.

(ii) $\mathrm{Ca + 2HCl \rightarrow CaCl_2 + H_2}$

Check: left Ca 1, H 2, Cl 2; right Ca 1, Cl 2, H 2. The equation is balanced.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the products formed when a piece of Sodium reacts with water. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The products are **sodium hydroxide (an alkaline solution) and hydrogen gas**.

$\mathrm{2Na + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2NaOH + H_2}$

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the element that is used for making coins and cups. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Silver (Ag)**: it is a hard-wearing, unreactive and lustrous metal, used for coins, trophies and cups.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select an element that gives a characteristic intense yellow flame colour. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Sodium (Na)**: sodium compounds give an intense, persistent golden-yellow flame in a flame test.
